About
Elon Musk is an engineer and entrepreneur who founded SpaceX in 2002 and has served as its chief executive officer, chief technical officer and chairman since May 2002. He has also been chief executive officer of Tesla since October 2008 and holds the title Technoking of Tesla. Source [ 1 ] Source [ 2 ]
Before SpaceX he co-founded Zip2, an internet software company acquired by Compaq in 1999, and founded X.com, which merged with Confinity in 2000 and became PayPal, acquired by eBay in October 2002. He was chairman of SolarCity from 2006 until Tesla acquired it in 2016, and was a co-chair of OpenAI at its 2015 launch before leaving its board in 2018. Source [ 1 ] Source [ 3 ] Source [ 4 ] Source [ 5 ] Source [ 6 ]
He co-founded Neuralink, a brain-computer interface company where he serves as CEO, and founded The Boring Company, a tunneling company. In 2022 he bought Twitter, now X, and in 2023 he started the AI company xAI, which acquired X in 2025. Source [ 2 ] Source [ 1 ] Source [ 7 ] Source [ 8 ] Source [ 9 ]
SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026 and went public on Nasdaq in June 2026, after which Musk held about 82 percent of its voting power. From January to May 2025 he led the Department of Government Efficiency in the Trump administration as a special government employee. Source [ 1 ] Source [ 10 ] Source [ 11 ]
Musk holds a B.A. in physics from the University of Pennsylvania and a B.S. in business from its Wharton School. He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2018 and named TIME's Person of the Year for 2021. Source [ 1 ] Source [ 12 ] Source [ 13 ]

28 of the major honors received by Elon Musk and his companies — from technical societies, governments and publications.
Robert A. Heinlein Memorial Award
2025

National Space Society
The National Space Society presented Musk its Robert A. Heinlein Memorial Award, its highest honor, recognizing SpaceX's transformative advances in reusable rockets, Starship, and the push to make humanity multiplanetary.

Most Innovative Company — SpaceX
2023

Fast Company
Fast Company ranked SpaceX the most innovative company in the world for 2023, citing the cadence of Falcon 9 reuse, the scale-up of Starlink, and progress on Starship — the engine room of Musk's space ambitions.

Member, National Academy of Engineering
2022

National Academy of Engineering
Musk was elected to the National Academy of Engineering, one of the highest professional honors for an engineer, for breakthrough contributions to reusable launch vehicles and electric vehicles.

Time Person of the Year
2021

Time Magazine
Time named Musk its Person of the Year for 2021, citing his reshaping of life on Earth and beyond through Tesla's electric-vehicle dominance and SpaceX's leadership in commercial spaceflight.

Person of the Year
2021

Financial Times
The Financial Times named Musk its Person of the Year for 2021, citing Tesla's trillion-dollar valuation and his outsized influence on markets, technology, and the global transition to electric vehicles.

Axel Springer SE

Fortune Magazine

Career Timeline of Elon Musk: Major Achievements and Milestones
Share:
By Popular Timelines Editorial Team
· Updated: July 14, 2026
Discover the career path of Elon Musk, from the first major opportunity to industry-changing achievements.
Elon Musk is a visionary entrepreneur and engineer known for his pivotal roles in revolutionizing the automotive and aerospace industries. As the CEO of Tesla, he has been instrumental in accelerating the global transition to electric vehicles and sustainable energy. Through SpaceX , he has disrupted the aerospace sector by developing reusable rocket technology and pursuing the ambitious goal of making humanity multi-planetary. Additionally, Musk has founded or led influential ventures such as Neuralink , focused on brain-computer interfaces, and The Boring Company, which aims to address urban congestion. His acquisition of the social media platform X (formerly Twitter) further underscores his significant, albeit controversial, influence on digital discourse. Musk is recognized for his high-risk, high-reward approach to engineering and his commitment to tackling complex global challenges through rapid technological innovation, positioning him as one of the most prominent and impactful figures in the modern tech landscape.

1983:
Sale of Blastar
In 1983, at the age of twelve, Elon Musk sold his self-programmed, BASIC-based video game titled Blastar to the publication PC and Office Technology magazine for a sum of approximately $500.
1994:
Internships at Silicon Valley Startups
In 1994, Elon Musk gained professional experience through two internships in Silicon Valley, working at Pinnacle Research Institute, which focused on electrolytic supercapacitors, and the startup Rocket Science Games.
1995:
Completion of Studies
By 1995, Elon Musk finished his period of study at the University of Pennsylvania , during which he also engaged in entrepreneurial activities like hosting parties and drafting a business plan for a book-scanning service.
Co-founding of Zip2
During 1995, Musk co-founded the web software company Zip2, marking one of his earliest significant business ventures.
Stanford Enrollment and Career Transition
In 1995, Musk was accepted into a materials science graduate program at Stanford University but chose not to enroll, instead attempting to enter the burgeoning internet industry by applying to Netscape while facing subsequent questions regarding his legal work authorization in the United States.
February 1999:
Compaq Acquisition of Zip2
In February 1999, the computer company Compaq acquired Zip2 for $307 million in cash, resulting in Elon Musk receiving $22 million for his 7-percent ownership stake in the company.
